{{Quote|Hello friends, my name is Sleightan and this is my, ah, er, droid L7-BO. ''[&hellip;]'' I'd like to sell him to ya, how about 3,000 credits? I know it may sound like a lot, but he is all I got left after the Empire took away everything I owned. What do ya say?|Sleightan, to a group of spacers at the Farrimmer Cafe|<ref name="Journal11" />}}
'''L7-BO''' was a [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] who, together with the elderly [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Sleightan]], formed a successful [[Con artist/Legends|con artist]] duo traveling between [[Space station/Legends|space stations]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Their scam routine involved Sleightan attempting to sell L7-BO to their marks while claiming that he had inherited the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] from his [[Death/Legends|deceased]] [[Armbrus|son]] and that he needed the [[Currency/Legends|money]] from such a sale to stave off poverty. After L7-BO was successfully sold, the droid would seek out any opportunity to sneak away from his new owners and return to Sleightan. At one point, the pair attempted their con at the [[Farrimmer Cafe]] [[Cantina/Legends|eatery]] aboard the [[Mynock 7 Space Station]], with Sleightan eventually selling L7-BO to a group of [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] and the droid subsequently attempting to slip away unnoticed while they were distracted by other events.

==Biography==
===The tale of tragic inheritance===
{{Quote|See, he used to belong to my son, Armbrus, who made his fortune as a pilot, flying things and people all over the Outer Rim for a price. ''[&hellip;]'' Well, the Imperials threw my son in a detention center, and then I get a note from one of those official-looking Imperial bureaucrats that said my son was killed while trying to escape. They confiscated my son's ship and took nearly everything on board except good old L7, which they said I could have. Seems the Imperials don't have much use for droids, and neither do I.|Sleightan|<ref name="Journal11" />}}
L7-BO, also referred to as L7, was a [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] who was active during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. He and the elderly [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Sleightan]] were successful [[Con artist/Legends|con artists]] who traveled from [[Space station/Legends|space station]] to [[Realspace/Legends|space]] station performing scams. As part of their con, Sleightan&mdash;who in reality was fairly [[Currency/Legends|affluent]] but presented himself as a down-on-his-luck [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]]&mdash;would claim that his [[Gender/Legends|son]], [[Armbrus]], had been an honest [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] working throughout the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. According to Sleightan's story, Armbrus was arrested by Imperial authorities on false charges and [[Prisoner/Legends|imprisoned]], and then [[Death/Legends|killed]] while supposedly trying to escape.<ref name="Journal11" />

Sleightan would further claim that L7-BO was the only thing from his son's [[Starship/Legends|starship]] that the Empire did not confiscate and allowed him to keep&mdash;with the con artist carrying a [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] on him with a forged Imperial letter on it that informed of the latter "fact." The old man would state to have no use for the [[Droid/Legends|droid]], who was purportedly his only possession of any real value, and then attempt to sell him to their marks in order to supposedly help himself fend off poverty. If asked, L7-BO would readily corroborate his partner's story about Armbrus, although he would tend to deliver it in a very dull manner. If the sale was successful, L7-BO would afterward attempt to surreptitiously leave his new owners and return to his partner-in-crime. Lessons that Sleightan learned during the pair's early attempts at their scam made him [[Programmer/Legends|program]] L7-BO so that he would only speak when spoken to.<ref name="Journal11" />

===The con at the Farrimmer Cafe===
{{RPG|"[[The Farrimmer Cafe]]"}}
{{Quote|Without my son sending me a few credits every month, things are getting a little tight. I figure if I could sell L7 for a fair price, I could use the money to make ends meet for a while.|Sleightan|<ref name="Journal11" />}}
[[File:Farrimmer_Cafe_SWJ11.jpg|thumb|right|300px|At one point, Sleightan and L7-BO attempted their con at the Farrimmer Cafe (pictured).]]
At one point, Sleightan and L7-BO traveled to the [[Mynock 7 Space Station]]<ref name="Journal11" /> of the Outer Rim's [[Mayagil sector/Legends|Mayagil sector]]<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for the [[Mynock 7 Station system/Legends|star system]] containing the [[Mynock 7 Space Station]]</ref> and entered the [[Farrimmer Cafe]], the only [[Cantina/Legends|eatery]] aboard the station&mdash;which L7-BO was very familiar with. Several moments later, the pair began striking up conversations with some of the cafe's patrons, specifically a group of six Human tourists who were passengers on a [[Luxury liner/Legends|space liner]] and a trio of [[Mriss/Legends|Mrissi]] [[Archaeologist/Legends|archaeologists]] who were looking for a wealthy patron for their excavations.<ref name="Journal11" />

Afterward, the two con artists approached the table of a group of spacers. Sleightan introduced himself and the droid and then offered to sell L7-BO for 3,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]], noting his belief that the droid would be of good use to the spacers. When asked, the man relayed to the spacers how he supposedly acquired L7-BO&mdash;noting, as part of his scam story, his belief that the Empire had no use for such a droid&mdash;and attempted to convince them that his need to sell the droid was sincere. Sleightan also informed the spacers that, in case they refused the offer, he would sell the droid to the Mrissi archaeologists, despite them not wishing to meet his asking price.<ref name="Journal11" />

The group of spacers haggled over the price with the con artist&mdash;which he only did grudgingly, claiming to really like L7-BO despite not having a real use for him and needing the money. In the end, Sleightan lowered the asking price to 2,250 credits, at which point the spacers agreed to buy the droid. Immediately after the sale, after his partner had departed the Farrimmer Cafe, L7-BO began plotting his return to him at the [[Hangar/Legends|docking bay]] of the Mynock 7 Space Station, and eventually the droid made an attempt to sneak away from the spacers while they were distracted by other events.<ref name="Journal11" />
{{Endgame}}

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|He is real smart and can speak a whole bunch of languages and knows all about aliens from all across the galaxy. Now I am sure that a group a space-faring fellas like yourselves could use a droid like this.|Sleightan, to a group of spacers at the Farrimmer Cafe|<ref name="Journal11" />}}
L7-BO had shiny [[Metal/Legends|metallic]] plating with a slight [[Color/Legends|blue]] tint to it as well as bright yellow [[Photoreceptor/Legends|video sensors]]. He could run at significant speeds as well as dodge, hide, and sneak, and he was skilled at moving through stores aboard the Mynock 7 Space Station in order to shake off pursuit.<ref name="Journal11" />

The droid was fluent in 4.5 million [[Language/Legends|languages]] and could converse in several million additional tongues. He had considerable knowledge of [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]] and cultures, [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] systems, and governments, with Sleightan characterizing him as "real smart" during his sham sales pitch of the droid. L7-BO acted polite and, during their con attempt at the Farrimmer Cafe, the droid walked several steps behind his partner, exhibiting patience while waiting for him to navigate around the eatery's tables. Overall, L7-BO left the impression of a properly functioning and well-maintained protocol droid. Although Sleightan admitted that 3,000 credits was a high asking price for the droid, he also claimed that the price was fair considering his supposed circumstances.<ref name="Journal11" />

Additionally, L7-BO was a skilled con artist and storyteller, as well as a very quick thinker. He was programmed to only speak when he was spoken to during his and Sleightan's con attempts, and his programming also included instructions to seek out any opportunities to sneak away from his new owners and return to Sleightan.<ref name="Journal11" />

==Behind the scenes==
===L7-BO's possible escape attempts===
[[File:StarWarsAdventureJournal11.jpg|thumb|right|250px|L7-BO was introduced in ''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 11.]]
L7-BO appeared in "[[The Farrimmer Cafe]]," a [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] source article authored by [[Jean Rabe]] and [[J. Allan Fawcett]] for use with [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' and published in the [[November]] [[1996]] [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 11|eleventh issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'' magazine. The droid appears in one of the relatively interconnected roleplaying adventure episodes presented in "The Farrimmer Cafe"&mdash;which this article assumes plays out as described&mdash;and the ''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' article suggests several points in that chain of scenarios at which he could attempt to utilize the player characters' being distracted in order to sneak away.<ref name="Journal11" />

The first such opportunity is presented when two dozen agitated and [[Diet/Legends|hungry]] [[zdrinbagh]] creatures escape from the Farrimmer Cafe's kitchen and attack the establishment's patrons. Under the cover of the chaos, L7-BO can edge toward the eatery's door and, if unnoticed, slip out, at which point he has effectively escaped the player characters' grasp. Alternatively, the droid can make his escape attempt during a shootout that erupts at the cafe when a group of [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] attempt to retrieve a valuable [[Heist at Randar Dowellin's stronghold|stolen]] [[Karltonian Fiskin]] [[Coin/Legends|coin]] that the Human [[Bon Seqours]] has brought into the establishment. Finally, another opportunity arises for L7-BO to slip away unnoticed during a brawl involving the player characters and the sore-loser [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Technician/Legends|mechanic]] [[Cecil]] over a game of [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] gone wrong.<ref name="Journal11" />

===Other scenarios===
{{Quote|Help, help, they are with those crazed Corellians and they are trying to disassemble me!|L7-BO, in a potential scenario where the player characters are pursuing him through the Mynock 7 Space Station|<ref name="Journal11" />}}
[[File:BnugorAndSnowball-AJ11.jpg|thumb|left|300px|L7-BO may serve as a translator during the Gammorrean Bnugor's (left) attempt to retrieve his escaped pet Snowball (upper right).]]
If L7-BO does not encounter an opportunity to sneak away, he tries to make one himself by complaining of pain in his [[servo-dio]] or another of his components, after which he attempts to leave in order to supposedly undergo repairs&mdash;which he claims to prefer take place at a local repair shop "just around the corner" in case any of the player characters offer to repair him. "The Farrimmer Cafe" notes that the gamemaster player is free to let the characters of the other players pursue the droid if they notice him attempting to slip away, but notes that they would find capturing him to be difficult due to his skill set. As a last resort during such a chase through the Mynock 7 Space Station, the fleeing con artist begins to yell for help from the inhabitants of the station, claiming that the player characters are in league with the trio of anti-technological [[Corellian/Legends|Corellians]] they have encountered in a prior scenario and that they therefore wish to dismantle him.<ref name="Journal11" />

In case L7-BO has not yet escaped by the time of the final scenario in "The Farrimmer Cafe"&mdash;which is described as a highly unusual situation&mdash;he translates for the player characters what the recently arrived non-[[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]]&ndash;speaking [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] [[Bnugor]] is telling them, that is, that his [[snuzzleguff]] pet [[Snowball (snuzzleguff)|Snowball]] has escaped into the Mynock 7 Space Station and that he has tracked the creature to the Farrimmer Cafe. The droid's visual [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] then dim slightly when he relays Bnugor's following comment&mdash;that the very fast, flying snuzzleguff is also carnivorous, very aggressive, and highly [[Poison/Legends|venomous]], and that additionally the mercenary wishes for the pet to be returned to him unharmed at all costs.<ref name="Journal11" />
